subject.title: [Feature]: Built-in auto-update with configurable schedule, confirmation, and post-update notification

question: Should OpenClaw core add a first-class updater workflow, and what approval, scheduling, channel-targeting, and post-restart reporting contract should it expose?
rationale: The remaining work affects package replacement, unattended updates, operator consent, persisted restart state, and cross-channel notifications, so the right config and security boundary cannot be chosen safely by cleanup automation.

options.title: Design core workflow on safe updater path
options.body: Add the requested workflow only after maintainers define the opt-in config, approval modes, notification routing, restart-state persistence, and update.run or external-updater execution boundary.

options.title: Keep core package auto-updater only
options.body: Leave update.auto as rollout/cadence policy and route confirmation or notification orchestration to user cron, agents, or plugins until a stronger core need is confirmed.

options.title: Narrow to related follow-ups
options.body: Split post-update hooks, UI discoverability, safe rollback, and plugin/skill auto-update into their existing narrower issues and close only if maintainers reject the broad core workflow.

recommendation.title: Design core workflow on safe updater path
recommendation.body: Add the requested workflow only after maintainers define the opt-in config, approval modes, notification routing, restart-state persistence, and update.run or external-updater execution boundary.

likelyOwner.reason: They introduced and recently carried the core updater surface that this feature would extend.
